decisionRules.keep: User-authored bytes or proven domain semantics are preserved, but never inherit Eva1 execution authority.
decisionRules.convert: A deterministic converter must create a typed Eva2 candidate with source provenance; activation may require owner confirmation.
decisionRules.archive-only: Retained only in the access-controlled recovery checkpoint or a later encrypted audit package; unavailable to normal model context and runtime authority.
decisionRules.rebuild: Discard legacy projection or runtime state and derive it again only from Eva2 authority or newly confirmed configuration.
decisionRules.delete-exclude: Excluded from every Eva2 import; physical removal or crypto-shred follows privacy, reachability, and rollback approval.
decisionRules.unspecified: Anything not explicitly selected by this manifest is excluded from Eva2.
decisionRules.overlapPrecedence: delete-exclude always wins over archive-only, rebuild, convert and glob overlap. Recovery custody never authorizes Eva2 import.

universalImportGates: ADR-0001 vertical gates are green before any data importer runs.
Every selected row has source database SHA-256, table, legacy primary key and canonical row hash.
The converter runs twice with byte-identical canonical JSONL and no model, connector or external I/O.
Every selected item has tenant/principal, provenance, privacy class, numeric retention and delete SLA.
Media and document bytes cannot leave the recovery checkpoint until their item-specific pre-copy or signed-selection gate is satisfied.

Legacy commitments cannot create runnable episodes until LegacyEffectReconciliation/v1 proves zero effects or fully reconciles every effect, delivery, artifact and current external readback; owner reauthorization alone is insufficient.
Importer rejects secrets, absolute host paths, executable payloads, test identities and unmapped relations.
Import into an empty installation is idempotent and creates no active effect or resumed work.
EvaPortableArchive/v1 restores into a second clean installation and a generic reader reconstructs the selected data while DBOS and Eva1 are absent.
Pre-import export/backup plus batch deletion and crypto-shred prove rollback and privacy erasure.
A release signing key signs the final row-level selection and converter output before migration.
